html:
Great Moravia was the first large West Slavic state, centred on the Morava river in what is now the Czech Republic and Slovakia, from about 833 to the early 900s. It is on the map for 900.

It began when Mojmír I of the Moravians joined his land with Nitra. His successor Rastislav, wanting a church free of Frankish bishops, asked Byzantium for teachers. In 863 Cyril and Methodius came, translated the liturgy into Slavonic and created the Glagolitic script.

Under Svatopluk I the state reached its largest size, taking in Bohemia, the land of the Czechs, and parts of Poland and Pannonia. It fought often with East Francia. After Svatopluk died in 894 it weakened, and around 906 the Magyars, newly settled on the Hungarian plain, destroyed it. The disciples of Methodius carried Slavonic writing to Bulgaria.
sum: Great Moravia was the first large West Slavic state, centred on the Morava river in what is now the Czech Republic and Slovakia, from about 833 to the early 900s. It is on the map for 900.
